solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fiasco central to Rhondda MP's quibbling

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of these words, spanning their join, so it is central to them

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the last two letters of the valley's name, MP's and the start of quibbling

explanation.surface: A Welsh MP's hair-splitting is said to lie at the heart of some political fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhondda is a Welsh valley constituency; the answer runs from the end of its name across MP's into quibbling.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is an event that fizzles out disappointingly, an anticlimactic flop, much as a fiasco is.

clue.text: Down in Paris is seeing round large stores

indicators.note: the dating word goes round the French phrase, holding it inside

parts.note: someone who is seeing another person dates them
the French slogan 'à bas' means 'down with'

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris feeling low is apparently seeing a lot of big department stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' is not sadness: it is the French protest cry 'à bas', down with.
explanation.definitionFit: Databases are large organised stores of information held on computer, a figurative sense of stores.

clue.text: Became acquainted with religious text in anthem

indicators.note: the scripture abbreviation is put in the meeting word

parts.note: to meet someone is to become acquainted with them
OT, the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone got to know a passage of scripture set within a church anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral composition, the same kind of church piece as an anthem.

clue.text: I get wound up about my bad Latin

definitions.note: the answer speaks as itself, a thing that has thread wound onto it

indicators.note: the apology word is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: slang apology, the same as saying oops

explanation.surface: Someone gets riled about their own poor Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' looks like annoyed; it is thread or film wound on.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a reel or cylinder on which thread, tape or film is wound.

clue.text: Device our compilers played about with at launch of Chambers?

indicators.note: letters that are played about with are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the launch of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Crossword setters fooled about with an instrument when the Chambers dictionary was launched.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary crossword compilers use, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultramicroscope is an optical instrument for viewing particles too small for an ordinary microscope.

clue.text: The ins and outs at the end of the summer …

definitions.meaning: reads as 'the details', but means a cricketer's innings and dismissals

definitions.text: at the end of the summer
definitions.meaning: the cricket season ends with summer, when the year's figures are totalled

explanation.surface: Someone reviews the details of how the summer finally went.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman goes in and gets out; dividing runs by dismissals over the season gives these figures. A 'summer' can also be one who sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Batting averages are cricket statistics, each player's runs per completed innings over a season.

clue.text: Originator of Peer Gynt Suite missing core point of writing cycles

indicators.note: the letters cycle round, some moving from the front to the back
the word Suite loses its middle letters, keeping only its ends

parts.note: with its middle gone only the first and last letters remain
a nib is the point of a pen

explanation.surface: The composer of the Peer Gynt Suite seems to be missing something central to writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Grieg wrote the Peer Gynt Suite, but the definition stops before Suite: the play itself was written by Ibsen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, the Norwegian dramatist, wrote the verse play Peer Gynt, for which Grieg later wrote music.

clue.text: … when heading off country maiden

parts.note: following on from the summer's end, 'when' is in August, abbreviated

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: rural means of the country, as opposed to the town

explanation.surface: Continuing the cricket picture: at summer's end a girl sets off into the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, so 'when' points back to the end of summer: in August.
explanation.definitionFit: Maiden as an adjective means first of its kind, as in a maiden voyage, the same as an inaugural one.

clue.text: US needs miracle to repair image

indicators.note: the letters must be mended, put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: America needs a miracle to fix its reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Image' reads as reputation in the surface, but means a likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulacre, an old form of simulacrum, is a likeness or representation of something.

clue.text: Trapeze artist very daring with this group?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: performing with ..., split as two words
second meaning: a group of nine performers

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer is what a reckless trapeze artist works with: no net.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is an ensemble of nine musicians, or music written for nine players.

clue.text: Dug in search of jumble as 'repayment'

parts.note: a dug is an animal's teat or udder, also called a tit
looking for something
tat is cheap junk, the stuff of a jumble sale

explanation.surface: Someone excavated through a rummage sale looking for repayment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dug' looks like a verb but is a noun, an old word for a teat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tit for tat means retaliation in kind, paying someone back with the same treatment.

clue.text: A government's trading with India: he's selling

definitions.note: a clause: the answer is the man who is doing the selling

indicators.note: one letter is traded for another: the A swaps in where India stood

parts.note: admin is short for administration, the government of the day
the letter A, taken as written

explanation.surface: A government trades with the country India, and someone is doing the selling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India' is the radio code for I, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An adman works in advertising, whose job is selling products to the public.

clue.text: Display minimum of turkey cuts one's needed to fill roll

indicators.note: the inner letters go inside the roll like a filling

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: the turkey letter cuts into the contraction, splitting it

parts.note: one is, or I'm

indicators.note: the minimum part of the word is its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A sandwich advert: the smallest bit of turkey is enough to fill a roll.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitmap is a computer image stored as a grid of pixels, the data behind what a screen displays.

clue.text: Willing auctioneers valued item like chocolate teapot?

definitions.meaning: bequeathing an auction house a prized lot in a will
the idiom for being useless, as such a teapot would be

explanation.surface: A will leaves the saleroom a prized item, as useful as a chocolate teapot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, willing an auctioneer a lot that will be desired is leaving them a lot; idiomatically the phrase means falling well short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that leaves a lot to be desired is unsatisfactory, and a chocolate teapot is the proverbial useless object.

clue.text: New chord vocalist's mastered ahead of improv jazz experiment

indicators.note: the first part comes before the jazz word
the singer has the chord within, held as one holds a thing mastered

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer; the 's that follows reads as 'has'

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters of chord

parts.note: taken as written, before the letters are rearranged
scat is improvised wordless jazz singing

explanation.surface: A singer has got the hang of a new chord before an improvised jazz session.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word reads as music, but the answer is the physics thought experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Schrödinger's cat is a thought experiment about a cat both alive and dead until observed, illustrating quantum superposition.

clue.text: Get this attached to bed? MD will do

definitions.meaning: the panel fixed at the top end of a bed frame
a managing director heads the board, so is a head of board

explanation.surface: A doctor will see to fitting something on your bed.
explanation.walkthrough: MD looks like a doctor but is a managing director, who heads a company's board.
explanation.definitionFit: A headboard is the upright panel at the head end of a bed, attached to its frame.

clue.text: Fine to use cracking old clues

indicators.note: the using word cracks the other letters open, sitting inside them

parts.note: keys, the solutions or clues to puzzles, taken here twice
to do drugs is to use them

explanation.surface: It is fine to use old clues to crack something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like the adjective meaning excellent, but signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Okey-dokey is a jaunty expression of agreement, like saying fine or all right.

clue.text: Mock theatre fitting put up

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rep is a repertory theatre
apt means suitable
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A theatre fitting is mocked up and put in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a verb or adjective but is the British school noun for a practice exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock in British schools is a practice examination, sat on a test paper.

clue.text: Kirk & co warped parsecs to stop alien fray close to Rigel

indicators.note: to stop something is to restrain it, here by holding it inside
the letters are warped out of shape into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, a parsec being an astronomical distance
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial
fabric that frays ravels

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a bright star in Orion; only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: Star Trek crew warp through parsecs to halt an alien fight near the star Rigel.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kirk commanded the starship Enterprise in Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirk and his crew journey through the galaxy, so they are travellers in space, as the definition's example suggests.

clue.text: See 12
Appropriated 2008 words from new Mayor Boris?

definitions.meaning: Thanks, Ken: TA, British slang for thank you, plus KEN, Johnson's farewell to Ken Livingstone, whom he replaced as London mayor in 2008

explanation.surface: In 2008 the new London mayor allegedly took something over.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson beat Ken Livingstone to become Mayor of London in 2008; TA is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken means seized or claimed, the sense in which the mayoralty was won from the predecessor.

clue.text: Not the sharpest tool in the drawer, as evidenced by wooden secateurs

definitions.text: Not the sharpest tool in the drawer

indicators.note: the answer is shown in these words, which carry it inside them

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the end of wooden and the start of secateurs

explanation.surface: A dull blade is proved by a pair of secateurs made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is the definition, and 'wooden' both hides the answer and suggests a blunt tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is not the sharpest tool in the drawer means they are slow-witted, i.e. stupid.

clue.text: See 11
Was coupling lost on board?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: paired, of animals breeding
second meaning: checkmated, the king beaten in chess

explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship or an affair aboard it; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both paired for breeding and checkmated in a chess game.

clue.text: To the rear a couple of thousand curtains may hang

indicators.note: the whole is turned to face backwards, read in reverse
the two letters hang either side like curtains around the middle

parts.note: two Ks, K being thousand
can, in its informal sense of being allowed

explanation.surface: Curtains are hung at the back of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtains' reads as drapes but signals the two letters framing the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the hang of something means acquiring the skill or knack for it.

clue.text: Parson, having got sorted, pipes up in church

indicators.note: letters that have been sorted are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vicar, having got things in order, speaks up during the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipes up' suggests speaking; it is the organ's pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ stop controls a rank of pipes on a church organ, drawn out to bring them into play.

clue.text: Bird shot, which is edited from interview

definitions.text: shot, which is edited from interview
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a TV cutaway of the interviewer nodding, edited in from interview footage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird shot' reads as shotgun pellets, but the two words belong to separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a seabird of the tern family and a television reaction shot of a nodding interviewer.

clue.text: He has expressed terms lacking in aspiration

definitions.text: He has expressed terms lacking in aspiration

indicators.note: aspiration is the H sound, so the letters lose their aitches

parts.note: taken as written, before its aitches go
to tender is to offer or put forward terms

explanation.surface: A man spells out his conditions without ambition, or in a dropped-aitch accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney from London's East End traditionally drops his aitches, saying 'e 'as for he has.
explanation.definitionFit: An East-Ender, a Londoner from the East End, typically speaks without sounding initial H, exactly what the clue describes.
